gate.noUnacceptableSideEffects: None observed. The change is confined to the decomposition recipe of one Task template and its own constraint sentence; no Skill, capability, tool provider or MCP server changed, so the task-coordination vs task-execution skill split is preserved (the diagnosis judged skill_fit adequate for the coordinator and both leaves keep their grants). The candidate adds only an ordering edge; it authors no artifact and weakens no criterion. gate.holdoutPerformanceAcceptable: Yes. Observed sample and holdout are distinct tasks, and no holdout cost growth is claimed (failure repair, no tool-call-reduction objective).
gate.resourceCostAcceptable: Acceptable. Four scripted sides (baseline and candidate for the coordinator sample, and the same for the holdout) under the deployment's own runtime limits; no maxTokens ceiling was declared because this deployment reports no token totals for business Runs, and the budget note records what the budget derives from. The reordering adds no work to any leaf — it removes a wasted completion run that failed on a missing input — so it strictly reduces wasted grading in this two-stage recipe.

tokenUsage.source: deriveTurnTokenUsage(@deepseek-ai/dsh-token-meter) over every completed turn/start..turn/end slice of every session that made a model request
tokenUsage.buckets: inputTokens is uncached prompt input (uncachedInputTokens); cacheReadTokens/cacheWriteTokens are null unless every measured turn reported them — a bucket no route reported is never rendered as zero
tokenUsage.attribution: a turn is attributed to the phase of its first request; turns the meter could not prove are counted, not imputed; a phase that completed no turn renders null buckets (its unreportedBuckets names them) and is listed in phasesWithoutCompletedTurns
